daily_brief: The European Union faces a major test of unity as interior ministers convene emergency talks following the Ceuta migration crisis, which saw an estimated 50,000-69,500 people cross from Morocco into the Spanish enclave last week, leaving at least 83 dead [BBC, Guardian, RFI]. Italy has temporarily suspended Schengen arrangements with Spain, backed by Finland and Denmark, while von der Leyen called for stronger border security. Meanwhile, US-Iran tensions remain elevated as President Trump insisted negotiations are ongoing despite Tehran's categorical denial, warning this is Iran's 'last chance before decapitation' [BBC, Globe and Mail, The Hindu]. A cargo vessel was struck by an 'unknown projectile' in the Strait of Hormuz [France 24], underscoring the fragility of the shipping corridor. In Ukraine, drone strikes killed at least six in Russia, targeting Wildberries warehouses near Moscow and St. Petersburg, while a separate drone struck a busy Black Sea beach killing seven including three children [BBC, France 24]. Europe's drought emergency deepened as the Rhine fell to record lows, threatening commercial shipping [BBC Europe], while wildfires forced 67,000 evacuations near Spokane, Washington, and killed two firefighting pilots in a mid-air collision in Greece [Al Jazeera, Globe and Mail, BBC].

top_stories.headline: EU Ministers Hold Emergency Talks as Ceuta Crisis Exposes Deep Divisions Over Migration
bullets: An estimated 50,000-69,500 migrants crossed from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta last week; Spanish officials report approximately 69,500 have since returned to Morocco
At least 83 people died during the crossings (72 confirmed on the Spanish side, 11 on the Moroccan side), with over 1,000 treated by health services
Italy temporarily suspended Schengen arrangements with Spain, backed by Finland and Denmark; Czech PM Babiš called for suspending Spain's Schengen membership
European Commission President von der Leyen called for stronger borders including 'physical barriers where needed,' while EU interior ministers convened emergency video talks on Tuesday

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Focused on EU institutional response and von der Leyen's call for united action

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Emphasized humanitarian toll and Ceuta leader's accusation that Morocco orchestrated the crisis

top_stories.headline: Trump Insists Iran Talks Underway Despite Tehran's Denial, Warns of 'Last Chance'
bullets: President Trump claimed negotiations with Iran are 'going on right now' and called this Iran's 'last chance' to reach a deal before escalation of US strikes
Iran's Foreign Ministry categorically denied any negotiations with the US, stating talks are only occurring with Oman over Strait of Hormuz passage
Trump said he called off 'massive attacks' including what would have been 'the biggest attack since World War II' at the request of Gulf allies including Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Qatar
A cargo vessel was struck by an 'unknown projectile' in the Strait of Hormuz off Oman's coast on Tuesday, according to UK maritime authorities

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Balanced presentation of contradictory US and Iranian statements

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Emphasized that contradictory statements suggest little prospect for diplomatic resolution

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Commentary piece argued the US is 'persisting with a war it has already lost'

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Focused on the Hormuz shipping incident as concrete development amid diplomatic uncertainty

top_stories.headline: Ukrainian Drone Strikes Kill at Least 12 Across Russia, Including Beach Attack on Civilians
bullets: A drone struck a busy Black Sea beach near Arkhipo-Osipovka in southern Russia, killing seven people including three children and injuring 40
Separate overnight strikes killed five people near Moscow and one near St. Petersburg, with warehouses linked to e-commerce giant Wildberries targeted for the second consecutive night
Ukraine has not commented on the beach strike; some Ukrainian sources claimed electronic warfare jammed the drone's signal, causing it to crash
Russian strikes on Ukraine killed at least four people, including an 89-year-old woman in Mykolaiv, with two girls aged 2 and 12 among the injured

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Presented both incidents with verified footage; noted uncertainty about beach drone's intended target

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Led with warehouse strikes; noted Finland briefly established aviation restriction area

top_stories.headline: Rhine Falls to Record Lows as Prolonged Heatwaves Strain Europe's Rivers and Firefighting Capacity
bullets: The Rhine reached record low levels in Cologne and Lobith (Germany-Netherlands border), with 44% of Rhine measuring stations and 78% of Danube stations recording extremely low water levels
Water depth at the critical Kaub chokepoint near Koblenz hit the 2018 record low of 25cm, threatening commercial shipping on one of Europe's busiest waterways
Two firefighting pilots (one Danish, one Greek officer) were killed when their helicopters collided mid-air while battling wildfires near Athens; a British pilot survived
Heatwaves above 40°C are forecast to continue across central and southern Europe for at least another week; wildfires in France uncovered buried WWII munitions

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Focused on economic implications for shipping and navigation

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Covered helicopter collision with emphasis on wildfire season dangers

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Linked helicopter crash to climate change creating longer fire weather periods; covered WWII shells discovery

top_stories.headline: Spokane Wildfires Destroy 700 Buildings, Force 67,000 to Evacuate in Washington State
bullets: Three fast-moving wildfires on Spokane's northern outskirts have burned over 8,000 acres (32 square kilometers) and destroyed more than 700 buildings since the weekend
Approximately 67,000 residents are under evacuation orders, up from 4,000 on Sunday, as fires spread from surrounding forests into residential neighborhoods
The fires are currently the top firefighting priority in the United States; no deaths have been confirmed but authorities say full damage assessment will take time
Calmer winds and lower temperatures arrived Monday to aid firefighters, but hot and dry conditions are expected to return by midweek

sources.name: Al Jazeera
sources.framing_note: Provided detailed explainer on why fires spread so rapidly; emphasized climate factors

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Led with human impact and resident accounts of devastation
